blind.description: A toppled, ancient classical column lying horizontally on its side. It consists of three fluted stone drums aligned in a row attached to a carved rectangular capital or base block at one end. The entire fallen structure rests on a bed of small rubble rocks and debris along the base. The surfaces are solid, stylized sculpted stone with weathered, chipped edges and tan/sandstone coloring.
blind.from_above: From directly above, it appears as a straight column section composed of a rectangular block at the top followed by three segmented fluted cylinders, with scattered rubble peeking out along the sides.
blind.extra_base_or_ground: small bed of rubble and loose stone debris underneath
blind.height_vs_figure: Lying low to the ground, about 1.3 to 1.5 feet high (roughly a quarter of the figure's height), with a total length of roughly 5 to 5.5 feet (close to the height of the figure) and width of about 1.5 to 2 feet.

notes: height slightly squatter than catalog target but reads cleanly as fallen column drums
